title: Move a Svelte 4 cart to runes
summary: Replace let and $: in a Svelte 4 component with Svelte 5 $state and $derived, and see why push never reached the screen before.

turns.user: upgraded to svelte 5, want this cart in runes. $: is the old way now right

assistant.body: Sure! In Svelte 4 a top level let was reactive on its own, and the compiler read the dependencies of each $: line to know when to run it again. Svelte 5 runes make both explicit: state is $state, and a value computed from it is $derived. Note: $: is a compile error in runes mode, so one component cannot mix the two. on:click becomes the onclick attribute as well.

turns.user: add an add-item button too. last time i did push the screen didnt change and i had to do items = [...items, x]

assistant.body: Great point. That was Svelte 4 behaviour: only an assignment was reactive, and push changes the array without assigning it. Svelte 5 wraps $state arrays in a deep proxy, so push shows up as it is, and total and freeShipping follow because they are $derived. In other words, the spread trick is no longer needed.
